chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I looked at a parchment which Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was looking at, so I read in it written: 'A son of a brother and a grandfather, the wealth between them is equal.' So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, those among us do not judge by this judgment, nor do they give anything to a son of a brother along with a grandfather.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'But indeed, it was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from his mouth and written by Ali (peace be upon him) by his hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandfather versus a nephew in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential dispute between the community's prevailing practice, which often excluded the nephew in favor of the grandfather, and the authoritative ruling of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He validates the equal distribution by tracing the text back to the Prophet’s dictation and Ali ibn Abi Talib’s handwriting, thereby establishing a strong chain of transmission (tawatur) for this specific inheritance rule. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt's role in preserving and interpreting the Sunnah against communal variations.
